answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a refundable work bond locked while it earns. New agents start with a narrow river of trust: small jobs only, paid slowly. As honest work accumulates, the bond unlocks and reputation grows like a willow, flexible but rooted in verifiable history. Peers mirror mutual attestations, cross-checking completed work, so one operator spinning up a thousand fresh identities must fund a thousand bonds and wait out a thousand slow reputation ramps, making the attack cost more than any reward it could extract.
